# THE DETACHMENT [italic]Lucky Thirteen. We make our own luck.[/italic]
## WHO WE ARE The garrison is a platoon of the United States Colonial Marine Corps, 4th Division, 13th Strike Group, 13th Regiment, known across the frontier as the Lucky Thirteen. Most of us are reservists from the inner United Americas colonies, called up after the Tychon Tackle and sent to the Neroid Sector because the insurgencies out here are growing faster than the Corps can answer them. We are not the Corps' finest. We are the ones who showed up.
## CHAIN OF COMMAND - [bold]Commanding Officer:[/bold] sets the alert state, the curfew and the security zones, and signs every order on this board. - [bold]Executive Officer:[/bold] runs the detachment day to day and receives civilian complaints in writing. - [bold]Staff Officers:[/bold] patrol schedules, checkpoint orders, supply, and liaison with Colony Administration. - [bold]Squad Sergeants and their squads:[/bold] the Marines you will see on your street.
## MISSION IAW the standing orders of the 13th Regiment, the detachment will: - defend the colony against dissident and insurgent attack, including cells operating under the Colonial Liberation Front name; - respond to fire, collapse, gas release and any other mass casualty event; - monitor the atmosphere and the perimeter and give early warning; - secure the colony's power, water, air and landing facilities.
## THE STABLE LESSON In 2168 Drill Site 68-B on Albacetire punctured a ravine of pressurised carbon monoxide. More than twelve thousand people died in the Carbon Ravine disaster, Marines among them. The Albacetire Stability Mandate built Joint Base Schaefer, the fort the locals call Stable, and taught every garrison in the sector what the Corps should have known already: the Marine at the gate is also the first responder.
## STANDING ORDERS TO MARINES Published so that civilians know what to expect from us, and so that you can hold us to it. - A Marine identifies himself and his unit when a colonist asks. - Nothing is taken from a civilian without a signed receipt. - Force is the last tool, not the first. Escalation is reported up the chain. - A Marine who breaks these orders answers to the Commanding Officer, not to his squad.
